# Complete session head public behavior
Two public exports only as in head-public-api.d.ts. Use actual listed dependency imports. No I/O or mutation of records. isObjectRecord accepts any nonnull nonarray object; readTrimmedString accepts actual strings only, trims, returns undefined for empty. deriveSessionTitle returns first50 UTF16 code units + "..." if longer, unchanged otherwise when attachments empty. Use that port rather than implement title yourself. Preserve existing Apache/NOTICE obligations; no MIT/legal claim.

Head: file order wins, no timestamp sort. For every visited entry evaluate user visibility then assistant visibility. First visible user OR assistant with nonempty cwd establishes workspace, fallback entry.cwd then message.cwd then request.cwd, trimmed strings only. Continue seeking workspace until set. First visible user stops traversal and returns own keys in order workspacePath, previewTitle, createdAt including explicit undefined fields. No visible user returns only own workspacePath key (even undefined). Head does NOT filter sidechain markers itself; separate marker export is diagnostic/gate for callers.

User requires entry.type exactly user and rejects entry.isMeta===true or message.isMeta===true. Message and request count as objects only by port guard. Content precedence message.content ?? request.prompt. Assistant requires type exactly assistant; reject entry.isApiErrorMessage===true or message.isApiErrorMessage===true or trimmed model <synthetic> (entry.model then message.model, first nonempty trimmed). Assistant only message.content. Markers are strict booleans; other truthy values don't suppress.

Content string: sanitize then nonempty visible. Nonarray/nonstring -> not visible. Array fragments: strings allowed both roles, nonobjects ignored; user ignores objects with type===tool_result and accepts other objects; assistant accepts objects only type===text. For object text choose nonempty trimmed text then nonempty trimmed content else empty; sanitize each. User joins nonempty fragments with double LF, assistant without separator. Sanitization: replace case-insensitive complete ide_opened_file blocks, and command/local-command-hyphen blocks, each by one space; then CRLF -> LF; trim. Matching is global, lazy across newlines; malformed/unclosed blocks survive. Compatibility literal patterns are /<ide_opened_file>[\s\S]*?<\/ide_opened_file>/gi and /<(?:local-command|command)-[^>]+>[\s\S]*?<\/(?:local-command|command)-[^>]+>/gi; closing name may differ, preserve this behavior. These are retained format literals, not a novelty/origin claim.

For ordinary decoded arrays preserve prior low-allocation requirement: no flatMap/filter intermediates, capture starting length once and skip absent/deleted slots (including inherited indexed slots when present). Extended JS inputs must preserve flatMap callback projection followed by filter(nonempty) and joining semantics: custom own flatMap, subclass/prototype/constructor/species behavior, proxies and global native-method/species changes are observable. Native-method/species references captured at module load for ordinary-array eligibility. On proxy inputs do not trigger extra get/has traps merely for optimizing; native sequence for Proxy(["x","y"]) is get flatMap,length,constructor; has0,get0,has1,get1. Mutating getters can delete next element or append: deleted original slots skipped, appended beyond captured length ignored. Native errors from getters/species/custom methods retain identity; do not catch/normalize. No fixed performance benchmark/novelty claim.

CreatedAt only first visible user's timestamp. Read candidate values before conversion, in order: entry.timestamp, createdAt, updatedAt, created_at, updated_at,time; message.timestamp,createdAt,updatedAt; request.timestamp. All these getters are evaluated before timestamp selection. Finite number >1e12 means Math.trunc milliseconds; else >1e9 means Math.trunc(number*1000) seconds; <=1e9 invalid. String: trim; empty invalid; finite Number(string) follows numeric threshold handling with no Date.parse fallback for finite-but-too-small numbers. Otherwise Date.parse string and accept finite result. Nonstring/nonnumeric invalid. First valid wins.

Sidechain export uses entries.some semantics: skips sparse holes, short circuits; for visited entry observe message/request object fields then strict true at entry.isSidechain or message.isSidechain or request.isSidechain. Invalid null record entries throw naturally; head for-of traverses holes as undefined so sparse entries throw rather than invent admission. No validation/error replacement added.
